Search
sûrch
v. (to look through in order to find; to examine thoroughly; rendering Hebrew chaqar, Greek ereunao)
From Old French cerchier, Latin circare, to go about. Scripture's searching runs both ways: God searches the heart that no man can read, and man is commanded to search the Scriptures that read him.

Biblical Definition

Search means to examine thoroughly rather than to glance, and Scripture makes God the first and most searching searcher. He claims the office as His own: “I the LORD search the heart, I try the reins, even to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings” (Jeremiah 17:10). The verse follows immediately upon the declaration that the heart is deceitful above all things and desperately wicked, and who can know it — the answer being that God can, and does. The believer's proper response is not concealment but invitation: “Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts” (Psalm 139:23). A man who has hidden nothing has nothing to lose by the searching. The Spirit's searching reaches further still, into God Himself: “the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God” (1 Corinthians 2:10), which is why the things freely given to us can be known at all. Turned toward the text, the verb becomes a command with a warning attached, for searching may be done wrongly: “Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me” (John 5:39). Men may search diligently and miss the One the search is about.

Webster 1828 Definition

To look over or through for the purpose of finding; to examine; to probe or explore. Scripture applies the word to God searching the heart, the Spirit searching the deep things of God, and men commanded to search the Scriptures that testify of Christ.

expand to see more

SEARCH, v.t. [Fr. chercher; L. circare, to go about.] To look over or through, for the purpose of finding something; to explore; to examine by inspection.

2. To inquire; to seek for; to look for; as, to search out the cause.

3. To probe; as, to search a wound.

4. To examine; to try; as, to search the heart.

SEARCH, v.i. To seek; to look for; to make inquiry; to make examination.

SEARCH, n. The act of seeking or looking for something; inquiry; examination; a seeking or looking for.

Key Scripture

Jeremiah 17:10 — "I the LORD search the heart, I try the reins, even to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings."

Psalm 139:23 — "Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts:"

1 Corinthians 2:10 — "But God hath revealed them unto us by his Spirit: for the Spirit searcheth all things, yea, the deep things of God."

John 5:39 — "Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me."

Modern Corruption

Searching the Scriptures has been recast as a hunt for whatever a reader finds meaningful, so that the text yields a private message rather than testifying of Christ and searching the reader.

expand to see more

The common modern method reverses the direction of the searching. A man comes to the text to find what it means to him, and the question of what it means is quietly retired. But John 5:39 was spoken to the most diligent searchers of their generation, men who knew the text and missed its subject, and our Lord's complaint is precisely that their searching terminated on itself. Scripture has an object, and the object is a Person; a search that does not arrive there has failed however industrious it was. Hebrews and the Psalms add the further point that the reader is not the examiner but the examined.

A second corruption runs opposite and is more respectable: the notion that the heart is finally unsearchable even by God — that motives are so tangled that no verdict on them is possible, and therefore none should be pronounced. Jeremiah 17:10 forecloses it. The heart is unsearchable by man, which is exactly why the LORD reserves the searching to Himself and renders to every man according to his ways. The believer's comfort is not that his heart escapes examination but that he may invite the Examiner, as David does, and be searched by One who has already provided a righteousness not his own.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew chaqar (to search out, examine) and bachan (to try, test as metal) supply the Old Testament sense; Greek ereunao (to search, examine) is used both of the Spirit searching the deep things of God and of men searching the Scriptures.

expand to see more

Hebrew chaqar (H2713) — to search out, examine thoroughly; used of searching a land, a matter, and a heart.

Hebrew bachan (H974) — to try, prove, test as a refiner tests metal; the trying of the reins in Jeremiah 17:10.

Hebrew kilyah (H3629) — reins, kidneys; the seat of the inward affections that God tries.

Greek ereunao (G2045) — to search, examine into; used of the Spirit and of the command in John 5:39.

Greek anakrino (G350) — to examine, to judge; the Berean word for examining the Scriptures daily.

Usage

"“I the LORD search the heart” — what is unsearchable to man is open to God."

"“Search me, O God, and know my heart” — the believer invites the examination he cannot escape."

"“They are they which testify of me” — a search that misses Christ has missed the point of the book."
